---
title: "Analysis 1: linear model per gene (tumor vs normal)"
format: html
execute:
  warning: false
---

## Load libraries

```{r}
#| message: false
library("tidyverse")
library("broom")
library("ggrepel")
```

## Load data

The wide file has about 16,600 gene columns, so each line is longer than
the default read buffer. The buffer is increased before reading.

```{r}
#| message: false
Sys.setenv("VROOM_CONNECTION_SIZE" = "5000000")

dat <- read_tsv("../data/03_dat_aug.tsv.gz")

probemap <- read_tsv(
  "../data/_raw/gencode.v36.annotation.gtf.gene.probemap"
) |>
  select(gene = id,
         symbol = gene)
```

## Paired or unpaired?

How many patients have both a tumor and a normal sample. If 20 or more we go
with the paired model.

With exactly 2 samples per patient, `log2_expr ~ condition + patient` is in
practice a paired t-test written as a linear model. The patient term removes
the differences between patients, so the condition effect is estimated from
the within-patient differences.
(This should probably be moved to 04_describe.qmd later.)

```{r}
paired_patients <- dat |>
  count(patient) |>
  filter(n == 2)

n_paired <- nrow(paired_patients)
n_paired

use_paired <- n_paired >= 20
```

## Condition as factor

normal is the reference level, so the coefficient is tumor minus normal.

```{r}
dat <- dat |>
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = c("normal", "tumor")))

if (use_paired) {
  dat <- dat |>
    semi_join(paired_patients, by = "patient")
}
```

## Long format

```{r}
dat_long <- dat |>
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("ENSG"),
               names_to = "gene",
               values_to = "log2_expr")
```

Test run on 100 random genes first. Set `test_run` to FALSE to run on all
genes (remember to do this before the final render).

```{r}
test_run <- FALSE

if (test_run) {
  set.seed(42)
  some_genes <- dat_long |>
    distinct(gene) |>
    slice_sample(n = 100)

  dat_long <- dat_long |>
    semi_join(some_genes, by = "gene")
}
```

## Nest by gene

```{r}
dat_nested <- dat_long |>
  group_by(gene) |>
  nest()

dat_nested
```

## One model per gene

```{r}
if (use_paired) {
  model_formula <- log2_expr ~ condition + patient
} else {
  model_formula <- log2_expr ~ condition
}

dat_nested <- dat_nested |>
  mutate(model_object = map(data,
                            ~ lm(model_formula, data = .x)))
```

## Tidy the models

```{r}
dat_nested <- dat_nested |>
  mutate(model_object_tidy = map(model_object,
                                 ~ tidy(.x,
                                        conf.int = TRUE,
                                        conf.level = 0.95)))
```

## Unnest and keep the condition term

```{r}
lm_results <- dat_nested |>
  unnest(model_object_tidy) |>
  filter(term == "conditiontumor") |>
  select(gene, estimate, std.error, statistic,
         p.value, conf.low, conf.high) |>
  ungroup()
```

## Add gene symbols

```{r}
lm_results <- lm_results |>
  left_join(probemap, by = "gene") |>
  relocate(symbol, .after = gene)
```

## Multiple testing

```{r}
lm_results <- lm_results |>
  mutate(q_value = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
         is_significant = case_when(q_value < 0.05 ~ "yes",
                                    TRUE ~ "no"))
```

The expression values are log2(CPM+1), i.e. normalised for library size,
so differences in sequencing depth between samples are not read as
differences in expression. The estimate can then be read directly as the
log2 fold change of tumor vs normal. E.g. an estimate of 2 means about 4
times higher expression in tumor.

## Direction of change

Up / Down if q < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1, otherwise NS.

```{r}
lm_results <- lm_results |>
  mutate(direction = case_when(q_value < 0.05 & estimate > 1 ~ "Up",
                               q_value < 0.05 & estimate < -1 ~ "Down",
                               TRUE ~ "NS"))

lm_results
```

Check for q values that are rounded to 0 (they would give Inf in the
volcano plot).

```{r}
lm_results |>
  filter(q_value == 0) |>
  count()
```

## Save results

```{r}
write_tsv(lm_results, "../data/05_dat_lm_results.tsv.gz")

lm_summary <- lm_results |>
  count(direction)

lm_summary

write_tsv(lm_summary, "../results/05_n_up_down.tsv")

n_tested <- nrow(lm_results)
n_down <- lm_results |>
  filter(direction == "Down") |>
  nrow()
n_up <- lm_results |>
  filter(direction == "Up") |>
  nrow()
pct_changed <- round(100 * (n_down + n_up) / n_tested)
```

In total `r format(n_tested, big.mark = ",")` genes were tested. With
q < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1, `r format(n_down, big.mark = ",")` genes are down
and `r format(n_up, big.mark = ",")` genes are up in tumor compared to
normal. So around `r pct_changed`% of the genes change.

Dead end: we first ran this without the CPM normalisation and got 7,164 down
and 1,625 up genes. Nearly all genes looked lower in tumor, most likely
because the normal samples were sequenced deeper, not because of biology.
That is why we added the library size normalisation.

## Volcano plot

Label the 10 significant genes with the lowest q value. If a gene has no
symbol the Ensembl ID is used instead.

```{r}
top_genes <- lm_results |>
  filter(direction != "NS") |>
  arrange(q_value) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

volcano_dat <- lm_results |>
  mutate(label = case_when(gene %in% pull(top_genes, gene) ~
                             coalesce(symbol, gene),
                           TRUE ~ ""))

volcano_plot <- volcano_dat |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate,
             y = -log10(pmax(q_value, 1e-300)),
             colour = direction,
             label = label)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text_repel(size = 3, max.overlaps = 20, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Down" = "steelblue",
                                 "NS" = "grey70",
                                 "Up" = "firebrick")) +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change (tumor vs normal)",
       y = "-log10(q value)",
       colour = "",
       title = "Differential expression, tumor vs normal") +
  theme_minimal()

volcano_plot

ggsave("../results/05_volcano.png", volcano_plot, width = 7, height = 5)
```

One point is one gene. On the x axis is the log2 fold change (tumor vs
normal), on the y axis -log10 of the q value, so higher means more
significant. The dashed lines are the cut-offs we used (q < 0.05 and
|log2FC| > 1).

Some of the most significant down genes are BEST4 and GUCA2B. In the
normal colon these are expressed by a specific cell type at the top of the
crypts, the BEST4+/OTOP2+ cells, and this cell type is changed in
inflammation and cancer (Parikh et al. 2019). GUCA2B codes for
uroguanylin. The related hormone guanylin was lost in almost all colorectal
tumors in Wilson et al. (2014). CA7 is also down, which fits with Yang et
al. (2015), who found lower CA7 in colorectal cancer tissue, linked to
poor differentiation.

Among the up genes, CDH3 was higher in all tumors compared to normal colon
in Kumara et al. (2017). KRT80 has been linked to migration and invasion
of colorectal cancer (Li et al. 2018), and was the most upregulated gene in
another TCGA RNA-seq study (Lin et al. 2020). ETV4 was overexpressed in
colorectal adenocarcinoma and confirmed in TCGA (Fonseca et al. 2021).

Our results are consistent with a loss of normal epithelial cell types in
the tumors, in particular the BEST4+/OTOP2+ cells, but bulk RNA-seq cannot
tell whether the cells are lost or only express these genes less.

## Forest plot of top genes

```{r}
forest_plot <- top_genes |>
  mutate(symbol = coalesce(symbol, gene),
         symbol = fct_reorder(symbol, estimate)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = symbol)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
                orientation = "y",
                width = 0.2) +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change (95% CI)",
       y = "",
       title = "Top 10 significant genes") +
  theme_minimal()

forest_plot

ggsave("../results/05_forest.png", forest_plot, width = 6, height = 4)
```

Here we show the log2 fold change and the 95% confidence interval for the
10 most significant genes. The intervals are narrow and none of them are
close to 0, so the mean difference between tumor and normal is estimated
precisely.
